_comment: TS↔Rust shared constants — parity by fixture, never by codegen or source scraping. Each entry declares its source of truth; hand-written tests on BOTH sides (src-tauri/src/parity_tests.rs via include_str!, src/lib/parity.test.ts via the real TS modules) assert their named constants equal these values, so a one-sided edit fails cargo test or bun test. scripts/check-parity.mjs (in the lint chain) validates this file's shape and that every entry key is referenced by both suites. endpointLocality is behavioral: the two implementations stay independent (security policy is never shared across the boundary) and the fixture pins the agreed verdicts.

secureOverlap.sourceOfTruth: src/ai/guard.ts containsPrivateDataOverlap ↔ src-tauri/src/secret.rs echoes_secure_text — the verbatim-phrase rule that stops ordinary private prose (which trips no secret pattern and carries no marker) from riding an outbound lane. Written twice on purpose, MIRROR-NOT-IMPORT, and pinned here. NOTE the one deliberate difference: TS normalizes NFKC first and Rust has no std normalizer, so every case below stays in NFC.

localAiAllowedCases.sourceOfTruth: behavioral: src-tauri/src/frontmatter_keys.rs local_ai_allowed (via owned_key) ↔ src/lib/frontmatterKeys.ts localAiAllowedOverride (the web vault's reader): only Rust's spelling grants, any spelling that says anything but true denies, a second line naming the key, or one holding a control character or U+FEFF, denies; where the frontmatter decodes as YAML the decoded value must agree; frontmatter that won't decode denies only when a line the line reader can't name mentions the key

protectionFlagCases.sourceOfTruth: behavioral: src-tauri/src/corpus.rs locked_field / secure_field ↔ src/lib/frontmatter.ts isLockedFrontmatter / isSecureFrontmatter: a lock or secure line in any spelling counts; locked only for `true`, secure for anything but `false` (Codex review of PR #303, items 2 and 7)

removeKeyCases.sourceOfTruth: behavioral: src-tauri/src/frontmatter_writes.rs remove_key ↔ src/lib/frontmatterWrites.ts removeKey: a key goes with its span (lines under it, a `? key`'s `: value` line), never from block text; a list item's next key takes its dash; a plain key only at the top level (Codex review of PR #303, items 4 and 8)

frontmatterDisagreementCases.sourceOfTruth: behavioral: every distinct input the frontmatter differential harness (scripts/frontmatter-differential.ts) found Rust and TypeScript reading differently: at 828f994d (1,276 distinct in 20,000 cases) and, with the pool widened to Unicode line breaks, BOM, NBSP, NUL, lone CRs and YAML 1.1 booleans, at e06d292e (1,604 distinct in 20,000), plus the review's named rows, pinned to the verdict both now give: body edit a/l/p/r, on-device t/f/u, locked 1/0, secure 1/0 (frontmatter_differential_tests.rs `verdict` ↔ the harness's `verdict`)
